kevin_rahman: Heads-up — saw a node (node-73) spitting repeated Xid 31/32 errors during the nightly training jobs. Can someone drop a terse checklist for oncall to collect logs + decide drain vs replace? Need paste-ready steps.

samir: Quick checklist I use: 1) Capture dmesg + journalctl around the time window. 2) Dump `nvidia-smi -q -d ERROR` + `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=...` 3) Capture pod/job ids that hit the node. 4) Check ECC counters and look for growing ECC values. 5) If > 3 Xid events in 1h or card ECC rising -> drain.

maria_ops: Paste-friendly script below — runs locally on node and uploads bundle to our infra S3 (internal). Use it in triage or attach to incident ticket. Replace S3 URL/env as needed.

samir: ```
#!/bin/bash
set -e
OUT=/tmp/gpu-triage-$(hostname)-$(date +%s)
mkdir -p "$OUT"
# kernel messages, show 200 lines around last error
dmesg -T | tail -n 100 > "$OUT"/dmesg.tail
journalctl -k --since "-30m" > "$OUT"/journalk.30m
journalctl -u kubelet --since "-30m" > "$OUT"/journal-kubelet.30m || true
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,ERROR,UTILIZATION > "$OUT"/nvidia-smi.q
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv > "$OUT"/nvidia-summary.csv
# grab Xid lines from dmesg/journal
dmesg -T | egrep -i "(xid|xid 31|xid 43|ecc)" > "$OUT"/xid.lines || true
journalctl -k --grep=Xid --since "-1h" > "$OUT"/journal-xid.1h || true
# attach pod list
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --field-selector spec.nodeName=$(hostname) -o wide > "$OUT"/pods.on.node
# bundle and upload (internal presigned cmd)
tar -czf /tmp/gpu-triage.bundle.tgz -C "$OUT" .
# NOTE: replace with our internal upload helper
infra-upload /tmp/gpu-triage.bundle.tgz || echo "upload-failed: attach /tmp/gpu-triage.bundle.tgz to ticket"
```

jen: Nice. Also add a 1-line triage rubric for oncall: "If Xid count >=3 in 1h OR any uncorrected ECC increments -> cordon+drain, replace GPU. If transient single Xid and no ECC delta -> monitor and increase sampling for 24h." Keep it short.

infra-bot: logging-helper v2 available — `loghook collect gpu --since 1h --bundle` will create same bundle and post to #gpu-telemetry with a presigned link. Use when possible to avoid manual upload. :gear:

maria_ops: I'll add the script + rubric to the runbook and link the `loghook` command. Oncall, when you open the ticket include: node name, gpu index (nvidia-smi output), job ids, time window, attach bundle, paste first 20 lines of `dmesg` and `nvidia-smi.q` and ECC counters.

kevin_rahman: Perfect — thanks. One more: any quick grep to find correlated network I/O errors? We saw an odd NIC drop around the same time.

samir: `journalctl -u kubelet --since "-30m" | egrep -i "(eth|link|carrier|netdev|rx error|tx error)"` and `dmesg | egrep -i "(eth|mellanox|mlx|net|link)"` usually surfaces driver-level drops. If NIC flaps + Xid spike, escalate to eng-networking.

jen: I'll make a tiny PR to the runbook with script + 1-liner rubric. tagging @maria_ops for review. :white_check_mark:
